parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to run a band recovery model like the one in BPA (Chp.8) and in trying to format the data, I've sort of gotten hung up on how to code individuals released and recovered in the same year/season. It seems like an individual has to survive from one year to the next before it can be recovered the way the model is written in BAP. Is that correct?  Otherwise, it seems like what BAP calls 'recovery at occasion 2' (pg 253) is what the MARK manual would call 'recovery on occasion 1'?

messages.subject: AW: direct recovery coding in state-space model (BAP Chp.8)
parts:
Hi Tim,

No worries about the spelling of BPA...

Regarding coding the capture-histories for a band recovery model: if an animal is marked and found dead in the same year, the capture history fragment gets 11. This means that the individual was released alive at occasion t and recovered dead at occasion t+1 (actually, since there is usually not a short and well defined recovery period, it means that the animal was found dead some when between release ccasion t and release occasion t+1), hence the probability of this fragment gets (1-s[t])*r[t]. You are right that in MARK the coding is different, because there are for each occasion two columns, one for the release and one for the potential recovery. In the actual case the recovery would also be at occasion t. The different coding has no effect on the parameter estimates, but the labelling of the recovery parameters is different.

Kind regards

Michael
